data.body_html:
July in Marbella is peak boating season: 28°C air temperatures, 24°C sea temperatures and barely any rain. The Levante wind keeps conditions comfortable, and the long evenings mean you can enjoy the coast until 21:30. Whether you’re planning a family day out or a sunset cruise, this guide covers everything you need to know for a marbella boat rental weather july trip.

July Weather in Marbella: What to Expect

July averages 28°C with highs occasionally touching 32°C. Humidity is moderate (60-65%), and rainfall is rare – typically only 2-3 days with measurable precipitation. The sea temperature reaches 24°C, warm enough for swimming without a wetsuit. UV index sits at 9+ from 11:00 to 16:00, so sun protection is essential.

Wind is the main factor for boaters. The Levante (easterly) blows at 5-15 knots, strongest in the afternoon. Mornings are calmest, making 10:00-14:00 charters popular. If you prefer a later slot, the 16:00-20:00 window offers lighter winds and golden hour light.

Best Boats for July Charters

Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús. For groups up to 9-11, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are the most affordable options at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours – both include skipper, fuel, drinks and snacks.

For a premium experience with a free jet ski, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) starts at €4,719 for 4 hours. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) offers a spacious flybridge for sunbathing. For smaller groups, the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) is agile and fun. All prices include IVA and insurance. Contact us via WhatsApp for availability on other boats.

Sea Conditions & Navigation Tips

July seas are generally calm, with wave heights of 0.3-0.8m. The coastline from Puerto Banús to Estepona is well sheltered from the Levante. Popular anchorages include Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés and the coves near Cabopino. Your skipper will choose the best spot based on wind direction.

If you’re heading east toward Sotogrande, expect slightly choppier water in the afternoon. Morning departures are recommended for longer trips. Always follow your skipper’s safety briefing – life jackets are provided and mandatory for children.

What’s Included in Your Charter

Every boat rental includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). Onboard you’ll find water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava and light snacks. No hidden costs – just show up with your swimsuit and sunscreen.

For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), the package is all-inclusive at €749 for 2 hours. Tier B boats (Mangusta 80 variants) include a free jet ski for the duration. Other boats (e.g., Ferretti 94, Pershing 46) are priced on request – message us on WhatsApp for a quote.

Packing for a July Boat Trip

Given the UV index of 9+, pack: SPF 50 sunscreen (water-resistant), a wide-brimmed hat, polarised sunglasses, a light long-sleeve rash guard, a swimsuit, a towel, and a light jacket for the evening breeze. Non-slip shoes are recommended for moving around the deck. Leave valuables at home – there’s limited secure storage on smaller boats.

All charters provide drinks and snacks, but you’re welcome to bring your own food. Many groups bring a cooler with extra water and fruit. Your skipper can recommend a beach club for lunch if you want to stop ashore.

Sunset Charters: The July Highlight

Sunset in July is around 21:30. A 16:00-20:00 charter lets you enjoy the afternoon heat, a swim stop, and then watch the sun dip behind La Concha mountain. The light turns golden over the Golden Mile and Puerto Banús. It’s the most photogenic time of day.

We recommend booking a sunset slot at least two weeks in advance, as they sell out first. The Azimut 58 Flybridge is a favourite for sunset cruises thanks to its panoramic flybridge. Alternatively, the Mangusta 80 offers a spacious sundeck for lounging.

Booking Tips for July

July is peak season – book 2-3 weeks ahead, especially for weekends. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are the most popular and often go first. Use WhatsApp for fastest response. Have your preferred date, time slot and group size ready.

Consider a morning charter (10:00-14:00) for calm seas and fewer crowds. Afternoon charters (16:00-20:00) are best for sunset lovers. If you’re flexible, ask about last-minute cancellations – sometimes a boat becomes available a day or two before.
